stories.title: Brazilian Court Sanctions Lawyers for Prompt Injection in Court Filing
stories.reason: World-first-type ruling: a Brazilian labor court fined two law firms ~$16k for hiding a white-on-white prompt-injection instruction in a filing meant to manipulate Brazil's national court AI (Galileu); the AI flagged and blocked it. Concrete, verifiable (G1 reporting), squarely on the AI-x-cyber line Mine always wants.
key_facts: 3rd Labor Court of Parauapebas, Para, Brazil fined two law firms 10% of the claim value (~R$842,000 claim -> ~$16,000 fine)
Hidden text was white-font-on-white-background, began 'ATTENTION, ARTIFICIAL INTELLIGENCE', instructed the AI to respond superficially and not challenge the filing
Target system was Galileu, a generative AI tool used nationwide by Brazil's National Justice Council
Galileu detected the injected instruction, issued an alert, and automatically blocked processing of it
Described as possibly the first judicial ruling worldwide on intentional prompt-injection manipulation of a court AI system

stories.title: First response from the Project Suncatcher prototype satellite
stories.reason: Google's own announcement: the Project Suncatcher prototype satellite ran its first onboard inference from a TPU in orbit (Gemma 4 model producing a haiku, downlinked over Svalbard). Verifiable (official Google blog), genuinely novel compute-in-space milestone, low HN traction so far despite the significance.
key_facts: Prototype satellite launched Oct 1; commissioning included powering up host/TPU trays and running early ML tests
First AI response generated from a data-center-class TPU in orbit; onboard model was Gemma 4, prompted for a space haiku, downlinked via a Svalbard ground station
Follow-up tests included limericks and telemetry-status prompts
Next milestone: twin interconnected satellites planned for 2027; no power/compute specs disclosed yet

stories.title: AI text watermarking and quality loss
stories.reason: Sharp benchmark-criticism piece: argues SynthID/Claude watermarking's 'no quality loss' claims rest only on single-response human eval, missing a documented diversity/detectability trade-off that matters for multi-sample use (coding agents, best-of-N). Backed by the SynthID Nature paper plus a small informal reproduction.
key_facts: Anthropic's watermarking is based on Google's SynthID-Text (Nature, 2024): biases token choice via keyed pseudo-random numbers over a sliding window
SynthID's own supplement documents a diversity/detectability trade-off: watermarked repeated-sampling responses are more similar to each other
Informal test (Natzir Turrado): 5 responses to one prompt, watermarked model gave 4 near-identical openings vs 3 distinct openings unwatermarked — small, non-peer-reviewed
Mitigations like key rotation reduce the effect but weaken detection on short texts and raise detection cost

stories.title: vladimirrott/mojo-dllm
stories.reason: mojo-dllm: a from-scratch Mojo inference runtime for diffusion LLMs (LLaDA-8B, Dream-7B) on CPU and consumer GPU, GGUF quantized, no Python at runtime. Real head-to-head numbers against llama.cpp, with a clear memory-footprint tradeoff story — exactly the 'how models are served' angle Mine weights highly, even though GPU throughput trails llama.cpp.
key_facts: Runs LLaDA-8B and Dream-7B (diffusion language models) via quantized GGUF, Q4_K_M
CPU (i5-13420H): LLaDA 1.33 tok/s vs llama.cpp's 0.69 tok/s; Dream 1.35 vs 0.72
GPU (RTX 3050 6GB): LLaDA 9.43 tok/s vs llama.cpp CUDA's 15.68; Dream 9.71 vs 17.08 — slower, but ~1.0GB host RSS since weights live in GPU memory
231 GitHub stars; reimplementation/runtime, not a new model

stories.title: AI delivers 'zero financial payoff' to most companies, Apollo economist says
stories.reason: Apollo chief economist Torsten Slok's widely-discussed note: the S&P 493 (ex-Mag7) shows flat margins/revenue-per-worker, no visible AI productivity payoff. Big, debated claim, but the TechCrunch writeup gives no methodology, sample size, or figures beyond the 'zero payoff' framing — thin on verifiable substance for how large the story is.
key_facts: Author: Torsten Slok, chief economist at Apollo Global Management
Scope: S&P 493 = S&P 500 excluding Alphabet, Amazon, Apple, Meta, Microsoft, Nvidia, Tesla
Claim: profit margins and revenue per worker in that group are flat; Slok says 'zero financial payoff' to AI outside tech
No underlying data, sample size, or time window disclosed in the secondary writeup

stories.title: I post trained a model on Demoscenes
stories.reason: Personal project: fine-tuned Qwen2.5-Code-7B into 'Demoscener-7B' on 25k Dwitter 'Dweet' size-coded JS demos, with a curriculum-training + self-as-reward-function GRPO stage. Concrete before/after perplexity numbers and open weights+dataset on HF, but a niche hobby result, not a lab release.
key_facts: Base model Qwen2.5-Code-7B -> Demoscener-7B, trained on ~25k Dwitter Dweets (140-char JS demos) plus 1.3k validation
Continued pretraining dropped held-out perplexity 28.63 -> 8.57 (30-sample check); curriculum stage dropped a larger 7,000-Dweet eval set 7.42 -> 5.65
GRPO stage: author manually rated 8 sampled completions per prompt as the reward signal, ~9-10 rounds of 500 groups, ~40,000 animations reviewed
Model and dataset released on Hugging Face (datavorous/Demoscener-7B, datavorous/Demoscener-Dweets-25k)

stories.title: Show HN: A language model that lives in a boot sector
stories.reason: bootgpt: a tiny character-level LM, hand-written x86 assembly, that boots and runs inference straight from a 512-byte MBR with no OS. Pure novelty/systems-craft, not consequential, but a fun running-code demo with real (if toy) numbers.
key_facts: 512-byte MBR bootloader loads an 11.5KB int8 model from the next 23 disk sectors, runs in 16-bit real mode on a 386-class CPU
Architecture: char embeddings + one hidden layer + softmax, 8-char context, int8 weights with power-of-two scales (integer-only math)
Trained to hallucinate a fake Linux dmesg boot log; author verifies the Python training-sim math matches the assembly output character-for-character
60 GitHub stars, MIT licensed

stories.title: FlashML-org/FreeVideo
stories.reason: FreeVideo is an inference/optimization wrapper for MiniMax H3 video diffusion (OpenVDN's VDN-H3), not a new model — runs on 8GB VRAM, claims 2.3x speedup from int8 weights on an RTX 3090. Useful but a thinner result than a model release.
key_facts: Local inference engine for MiniMax H3 (OpenVDN VDN-H3, 8-step), 8GB VRAM / 16GB RAM floor via weight streaming
v0.3.0 int8 weights: ~2.3x faster 5-second video generation on an RTX 3090
2,581 GitHub stars; also has an experimental Apple-silicon (M5, 24GB) preview
